_meta.indication: Radical cure (prevention of relapse) of Plasmodium vivax malaria in patients aged 16 years and older who are receiving appropriate antimalarial therapy for acute P. vivax infection; NOT indicated for treatment of acute P. vivax malaria

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; all patients received chloroquine plus either a single dose of tafenoquine (n=260), active control (n=129), or placebo (n=133) in a 2:1:1 fashion
pivotal_trials.population: Adults positive for P. vivax malaria (mean age 35, range 16 to 79 years), receiving chloroquine for the acute infection; G6PD-deficient patients excluded
pivotal_trials.n: 522 adults (tafenoquine/chloroquine n=260, placebo/chloroquine n=133, active control n=129)
pivotal_trials.result: Recurrence-free efficacy at 6 months 60% (155/260) with tafenoquine/chloroquine vs 26% (35/133) with placebo/chloroquine; OR 0.24 (95% CI 0.15, 0.38), p<0.001; risk of recurrence reduced by 75.9% (95% CI 61.8%, 84.8%)

key_safety: Common adverse reactions (≥5%): dizziness, nausea, vomiting, headache, and decreased hemoglobin. In Trial 1, dizziness 8% vs 3%, nausea 6% vs 7%, vomiting 6% vs 5%, decreased hemoglobin 5% vs 2%, headache 5% vs 7% (KRINTAFEL+chloroquine vs chloroquine). Main safety risk is hemolytic anemia in G6PD-deficient patients; asymptomatic methemoglobinemia also observed.
target_moa: Tafenoquine is an 8-aminoquinoline antimalarial that eradicates P. vivax liver hypnozoites (dormant liver stage), preventing relapse of malaria; exact mechanism is not known
companion_dx_detail: No named companion diagnostic device; G6PD deficiency testing is required before prescribing but no specific test is designated as a companion diagnostic

advisory_committee.vote: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (July 12, 2018): voted Yes 13, No 0 on substantial evidence of effectiveness; Yes 12, No 1 on adequate evidence of safety

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation for TQ for the radical cure of P. vivax malaria

citations.quote: TQ for the radical cure of *P. vivax* malaria has orphan drug designation.

summary.text: KRINTAFEL was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA with Priority Review, and had received Breakthrough Therapy and orphan drug designations. Pivotal evidence of effectiveness was supported by one Phase 3 trial (Study TAF112582, Part 2) (not accelerated approval), supported by a favorable Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee vote.
